name: Medusa
author: Erin Carter
description: Three translucent jellyfish bells cross a near-black water gradient at staggered depths, each dome glowing from a brighter contraction rim and trailing four faded tentacle curves. The bells are the only light: each one pulses on its own slow private cycle — a quick contraction with a small forward hop and rim flare, then a long relaxed glide-and-sink — while drifting along diagonal lanes that fade to nothing offscreen.

params.label: Pulse speed
params.effect: Scales every bell's contraction-cycle rate — higher makes the swim pulses, hops, and rim flares come faster.

params.label: Bell size
params.effect: Dome radius in CSS pixels; all bells scale together (tentacle lengths follow) while keeping their drift lanes.

params.label: Bells
params.effect: How many jellyfish bells swim the frame at once.

params.label: Bell brightness
params.effect: Overall emission of the bells and their tentacles; raises the jellies clear of the dark water.

params.label: Tentacle lag
params.effect: Phase delay, as a fraction of one pulse, between a bell's contraction and the whip of its tentacle curves — 0 moves them rigidly with the bell, 1 drags them a full pulse behind.
